question: Examine if the function $f(x) = \begin{cases} \sin(\pi x), & 0 \leq x < 1 \\ x^2 - 1, & 1 \leq x \leq 2 \end{cases}$ is continuous at $x = 1$.
explanation:
To check continuity at $x=1$:

Left hand limit:

$\displaystyle \lim_{x \to 1^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 1^-} \sin(\pi x) = \sin(\pi) = 0$

Right hand limit:

$\displaystyle \lim_{x \to 1^+} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 1^+} (x^2-1) = 1^2 - 1 = 0$

$f(1) = 1^2 - 1 = 0$

As LHL = RHL = $f(1)$, $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=1$.

options.A: No, it is discontinuous at $x=1$ because the left-hand limit is $1$
options.B: Yes, it is continuous at $x=1$ because LHL = RHL = $f(1)=0$
options.C: No, it is discontinuous at $x=1$ because $f(1)$ is not defined
options.D: Yes, it is continuous at $x=1$ because LHL = RHL = $1$
